sections.h2: Who can claim the Arizona homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Any adult resident of Arizona can hold the exemption, whether married or single. The statute asks only that the person be at least eighteen years old and live in the state, and that the property be one the person actually lives in.

Three kinds of homes qualify. One is the person's interest in a single compact piece of land with a dwelling on it. Another is one condominium or cooperative unit. The third is a mobile home, park model, motor home, travel trailer, fifth wheel, houseboat, manufactured home or other shelter, plus the land under it.

A married couple or a single person gets one homestead only. The dollar figure measures the equity of the person or couple, not the home's price. If spouses lived in a home together and later divorce, the total protected for that residence cannot go above the statutory cap, no matter how the equity is split between them.

sections.h2: Do I have to file anything to get homestead protection?
sections.html:
No. The exemption exists by operation of law, so no written claim and no recording is needed to hold it. That surprises many owners, since some states require a filed declaration.

A filing matters in one situation. If you own more than one property that might fit, a creditor can send a demand letter by certified mail, return receipt requested, asking you to say which one is your homestead. You then have thirty days from receiving the letter to answer. You can answer by recording a homestead exemption with the county recorder where the property sits, or by sending the creditor a certified letter, return receipt requested.

If you ignore that letter, you can later assert the exemption only by recording a claim with the recorder. Anyone who receives a demand letter while trying to sell should treat the thirty days seriously and may want a lawyer to review the response.

sections.h2: What debts can still reach a homestead in Arizona?
sections.html:
The exemption blocks forced sale under most judgments and liens, but several claims get past it. The statute lists the exceptions, and a mortgage or deed of trust tops the list, because a lender you agreed to pay can still foreclose.

  • A consensual lien such as a mortgage or deed of trust, or a contract of conveyance.
  • A lien for labor or materials, claimed under the mechanics lien statute.
  • A lien for child support or spousal maintenance arrears, if the arrears were reduced to judgment, a lien exists under the family law statute, or the court ordered a specific security interest.
  • A recorded civil judgment or other involuntary lien, but only to the extent your equity is more than the exemption amount.

A sale that the exemption should have blocked is invalid and conveys no interest in the homestead. A court deciding a contempt case on unpaid support may also treat the exempt portion as a resource the payer could draw on.

sections.h2: How does a judgment creditor force a sale when equity is high?
sections.html:
A judgment creditor that is not a mortgage lender can ask for a judicial sale only when the debtor's interest exceeds the homestead amount plus all prior consensual liens. The officer running the sale cannot accept a bid unless it covers the debtor's homestead amount, the prior liens and the allowed costs of sale.

If a sufficient bid arrives, the proceeds are paid in a set order. The debtor receives the homestead amount first, then prior liens are paid, then costs, and whatever remains goes toward the judgment. If no sale happens, because the creditor drops the attempt or no one bids enough, the creditor cannot add sale costs or attorney fees to the judgment.

The practical lesson is that the exemption protects a set slice of equity and leaves the rest open to a creditor with a judgment.

sections.h2: What happens to my homestead protection after I sell?
sections.html:
The protection follows the cash. It attaches automatically to your interest in identifiable cash proceeds from a voluntary or forced sale and lasts eighteen months from the sale date, or until you set up a new homestead with the money, whichever comes first. It does not attach to cash taken out in a refinance.

Two practical points flow from this. First, keep sale proceeds identifiable, for example in a separate account, because the statute protects only identifiable cash proceeds. Second, the parties may rely on the valuation shown in the final closing disclosure when deciding how much equity existed on a sale or whether a refinance returned cash.

Only one homestead at a time may be held, so an owner who buys a replacement home before the eighteen months run out moves the protection to the new property.

sections.h2: When does Arizona treat a homestead as abandoned?
sections.html:
A homestead is abandoned by a recorded declaration, by deeding the property away or contracting to convey it, or by permanently moving out of the home or the state. Moving out temporarily does not end it, since a claimant may be away for up to two years without losing the exemption.

A declaration of abandonment or waiver must be signed and acknowledged by the claimant, and it takes effect only when recorded with the county recorder where the property is located. A recorded mortgage or deed of trust is not affected by the homestead claim at all.

One detail helps estate planners. Moving the home into a trust does not count as abandonment when the claimant keeps the power to run and revoke that trust.

EventEffect on the exemption
Recorded declaration of abandonmentEnds it from the recording date
Deed or contract to convey the propertyEnds it, except a transfer to a revocable trust you control
Moving out for up to two yearsDoes not end it
Permanent move from the home or stateEnds it
Sale of the homeMoves to identifiable proceeds for up to eighteen months

sections.h2: Is the homestead exemption the same as a property tax break?
sections.html:
No. The homestead exemption in title 33 protects equity from creditors, while property tax exemptions in title 42 reduce what the county bills, and they have different rules and different offices. Tax exemptions for widows, widowers, owners with disabilities and some veterans are filed with the county assessor by affidavit.

If you are bankrupt or may be, the statute adds a rule: the exemption amount is fixed as of the day the bankruptcy petition is filed. If the equity is at or below the cap on that date, the home is fully exempt, and later gains in value during the case stay exempt too.

The dollar cap also adjusts each January 1 for the consumer price index, rounded up to the nearest $100, so the figure you see quoted may be out of date. Check the current number with an attorney or the legislature's posted statute before relying on it.

sections.h2: How does this affect selling an Arizona house for cash?
sections.html:
An owner whose equity sits below the statutory cap has all of it protected from judgment creditors, so the homestead rules themselves rarely block a sale. The questions that deserve a closer look are liens that survive the exemption and what happens to the money afterward.

  • Order a title search early so mortgages, mechanics liens, support liens and recorded judgments are known before you agree on a price.
  • Ask the escrow officer how each lien will be paid from the proceeds.
  • If a creditor sent you a certified demand letter, note the thirty day response window.
  • Keep the proceeds in an identifiable account if you want the eighteen month protection.

A cash buyer can close without waiting for a lender, which helps when a lien payoff date is close. This page is general information, so have a lawyer review a specific situation before you sign.

faqs.q: Is the Arizona homestead exemption automatic?
faqs.a: Yes. It exists by operation of law, so no recording or written claim is needed unless a creditor demands that you designate which of several properties is your homestead.

faqs.q: How long does homestead protection last on sale proceeds in Arizona?
faqs.a: It lasts eighteen months after the sale, or until you establish a new homestead with the proceeds, whichever is shorter. It does not cover cash from a refinance.

faqs.q: Can a mortgage lender foreclose on an Arizona homestead?
faqs.a: Yes. A mortgage or deed of trust is a consensual lien, and the exemption does not defeat it.

faqs.q: Can I leave my Arizona home for a while without losing the exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. A claimant may live away from the homestead for up to two years without abandoning it, but a permanent move from the home or the state does end the exemption.

faqs.q: Does a divorce change the homestead cap?
faqs.a: The cap does not double. For a home a couple shared before divorcing, the total exemption for that residence cannot exceed the statutory amount for either or both former spouses.
